tasks.title: JSON Schemas for the model, issues and theme files
tasks.description:
Write the three JSON Schemas (draft 2020-12) that define archmap's file contracts, following docs/design.md section 5 exactly.

- schema/archmap-model.schema.json: meta (schemaVersion, project, commit, generatedAt, repoUrl, profile, sources, coverage),
  zones, nodes, edges, entities (fields with provenance declared|observed|inferred), relations (cardinality 1-1|1-n|n-m,
  kind fk|join|name-convention), access (ops is a non-empty subset of "CRUD"), sequences (step grammar: message {m,k,t,d,r,ret?,i?},
  fragment {frag: alt|else|opt|loop|end, t}, note {note, t, tone}), views. Edge type enum: api, static, auth, pull, sql, cache,
  persist, call, link, deploy, event, queue. Edge confidence: verified|inferred|external. Optional edge "foundBy":
  static|llm|introspection (design section 14.3). Evidence item: {path, lines} where lines is "N" or "N-M".
- schema/archmap-issues.schema.json: {id, sev high|med|low, category security|data|reliability|performance|design|docs, title,
  anchor (exactly one of node|edge|entity|step), summary, impact, fix, detail?, evidence, source archmap|audit, track?}.
- schema/archmap-theme.schema.json: fonts, chrome and accent only. Relation, zone and severity colours are fixed (D10) and must
  NOT be themeable.

Rules: readers tolerate unknown keys, so do not set additionalProperties:false on objects (compatibility, design section 5).
Evidence is required (minItems 1) on nodes and edges. Keep to a small keyword subset that validate.mjs (next task) will
interpret without npm deps: type, required, properties, items, enum, const, pattern, minItems, minLength, oneOf, $ref to
local $defs. No format, no if/then, no remote $ref.
Referential checks (dangling ids) are NOT expressible here; they belong to validate.mjs.

add: tests/schema.test.mjs: each schema parses, declares draft 2020-12 $schema and an $id, and its required keys, enums and $defs match docs/design.md section 5

outcome.technical: Wrote tests/schema.test.mjs first (12 cases s1-s12, with a small interpreter for the agreed keyword subset), then saw it fail because the schema files were missing. I then wrote schema/archmap-model.schema.json, archmap-issues.schema.json and archmap-theme.schema.json (draft 2020-12, each with an $id). The only keywords they use are type, required, properties, items, enum, const, pattern, minItems, minLength, oneOf and local $defs refs. None sets additionalProperties. Evidence has minItems 1 on nodes, edges and issues, and lines matches ^[0-9]+(-[0-9]+)?$. access.ops matches ^(?!.*(.).*\1)[CRUD]+$, a non-empty subset with no repeats. Steps are a oneOf of message, fragment and note. An issue anchor is a oneOf of four single-key shapes. The theme declares only fonts, chrome and accent. Decisions the design left open: the model requires meta, zones, nodes and edges, and the other arrays are optional. The issues file root is {schemaVersion?, issues:[...]}, with the issue shape in $defs.issue. Theme accent is a #rrggbb string. I used the interpreter in the test only to check the schemas; it is not a dependency. The `writing-javascript` skill the brief lists does not exist (Unknown skill), so only test-driven-development was invoked. Dependants: docs/design.md names the three schema files by basename only, so it is still correct. Nothing imports tests/schema.test.mjs.
outcome.descriptive: Adds the three archmap JSON Schemas (model, issues, theme) and a 12-case test suite that locks them to design section 5.

verifiedBy: 12 cases in tests/schema.test.mjs. They check that each schema parses, declares draft 2020-12 and an $id, and that its required keys, enums and $defs match design section 5. They also check evidence minItems, the lines pattern, the ops subset, the step grammar, issue anchors and theme scope, and that no schema sets additionalProperties or uses a keyword outside the subset.

tasks.title: validate.mjs: schema subset, referential integrity and evidence checks
tasks.description:
Implement scripts/validate.mjs (Node >= 18, ESM, zero npm deps) and a tiny JSON Schema subset interpreter in
scripts/lib/jsonschema.mjs that supports exactly the keywords P1.1's schemas use (type, required, properties, items, enum,
const, pattern, minItems, minLength, oneOf, local $ref). Unknown keys in data are allowed.

CLI: node scripts/validate.mjs <model.json> [--issues <issues.json>] [--repo <dir>] [--json]
Checks, each finding with a JSON pointer and a stable code:
1. Schema: the model against schema/archmap-model.schema.json, the issues file against archmap-issues.schema.json.
2. Referential integrity: node.zone, zone.parent, edge.from/to, entity.store (a node id), field.fk and relations
   entity/field pairs, access.node/entity, sequence participant node and step m[] ids, note ids, view filters,
   issue anchors (node|edge|entity|"<seqId>:<stepIndex>"), step i (issue id, only when --issues is given). Duplicate ids.
3. Evidence (design section 14.3, borrowed from show-me): with --repo, for each evidence {path, lines} run
   `git -C <repo> cat-file -e <meta.commit>:<path>` and check the line range is within the file at that commit
   (git show). Without --repo the check is skipped and the output says so - it is never a silent pass.
Export a validate(model, {issues, repo}) function returning {ok, findings[]} so later scripts (merge, render) reuse it.
Output: human-readable by default, --json for machines. Exit 0 valid, 1 findings, 2 usage or unreadable input.
Use small inline fixtures and a throwaway git repo created in os.tmpdir() in the tests; do not depend on P1.3's golden model.

add: tests/validate.test.mjs: accepts a minimal valid model; rejects dangling zone/node/entity/participant/issue-anchor ids, missing evidence, malformed lines ranges and ops outside CRUD; with --repo and meta.commit, reports evidence paths missing at that commit and line ranges past end of file; exit codes 0 valid / 1 findings / 2 usage

outcome.technical: Wrote tests/validate.test.mjs first (21 cases v1-v21, red: module not found), then scripts/lib/jsonschema.mjs (validateSchema: type, required, properties, items, enum, const, pattern, minItems, minLength, oneOf, local $defs $ref; JSON-pointer errors) and scripts/validate.mjs (exports validate(model,{issues,repo}) -> {ok,findings[{code,pointer,message}],evidence:'checked'|'skipped'}; CLI with --issues/--repo/--json; exit 0/1/2). Codes: schema, duplicate-id, dangling-ref, evidence-lines-malformed, evidence-path-missing, evidence-lines-out-of-range, commit-missing. Integrity covers zone/parent/node.zone/edge ends/entity.store/fk/relations/access/participant node/step m[] and note ids/step i (only with issues)/view filters/issue anchors incl. seqId:stepIndex/duplicates. Evidence uses git cat-file -e <commit>:<path> then cat-file blob (rejects directories) for the line count; an unknown meta.commit gives one commit-missing finding; without --repo the output states evidence was skipped. Evidence is also checked on issues files. Ran: `node --test tests/validate.test.mjs` 21 pass 0 fail; full `node --test` 35 pass 0 fail (exit code not captured by my shell pipeline; the tally shows fail 0). Dependants: schema/archmap-issues.schema.json only names validate.mjs in a description (dangling step ids checked there, not in the schema) - still correct, validate.mjs checks step i against issues; tests/schema.test.mjs only mentions validate.mjs in a comment about the keyword subset - still correct, jsonschema.mjs uses exactly that subset and the full suite passes; docs/design.md names validate.mjs for the 14.3 evidence check - still correct, implemented as described (git cat-file -e at meta.commit plus line range; blob read instead of git show to reject directories). Exploration note: I read the two schemas and docs/design.md 14.3 (not in the brief) to know the model shape. Skill writing-javascript was skipped as the orchestrator instructed.
outcome.descriptive: Adds the archmap validator: schema subset interpreter, referential-integrity and duplicate-id checks, and evidence checks at meta.commit, with a reusable validate() export and a 0/1/2 exit-code CLI.

tasks.title: Anonymised golden model fixture derived from the private reference
tasks.description:
Hand-write the golden fixture: an archmap model of the reference app, a FastAPI + React + DuckDB dashboard that pulls
from an upstream data platform. Derive it from the single HTML file in .private/reference/, which you may READ but
must never copy, quote or name in any tracked file - not even its filename. THIS REPO IS PUBLIC.

Anonymisation rules (all mandatory):
- Use a fictional project name ("Northwind Insights"), fictional org, and generic repo paths (backend/app/..., frontend/src/...).
  Keep the architecture's shape: zones, the node set, the typed edges, the entities and fields, the 7 sequences and the step grammar.
- The upstream data platform, the SSO proxy, the lab-notebook vendor and any client product, site or table names become
  generic names ("Upstream data platform", "Corporate SSO proxy", "External lab notebook"). No client names, people,
  hostnames, URLs, dataset ids, RIDs or env var values.
- meta.repoUrl is https://example.invalid/northwind-insights; meta.commit is a fixed fake sha.
- Evidence keeps the {path, lines} shape with the anonymised paths. The golden test therefore runs validate WITHOUT --repo.
- issues.json: do NOT carry over the reference's issues. Write 6-8 synthetic, generic issues, one per category, anchored to
  fixture ids, each as class + consequence + fix only - no reproduction steps, no exploit detail, empty or generic `detail`.
- Before finishing, grep every file you wrote against .private/anonymise-denylist.txt and report zero hits.
The fixture is the ground truth P2's renderer will be compared against, so it must be rich: all zone kinds the reference
uses, C4 levels 1-3, async edges, CRUD access rows, name-convention relations with provenance inferred.

tasks.title: Vendor elkjs 0.12.0 and write layout.mjs
tasks.description:
1. Vendor elkjs 0.12.0 exactly (released 2026-07-17; newer versions are under two weeks old and are NOT allowed):
   `npm pack elkjs@0.12.0` in a temp dir, copy lib/elk.bundled.js to assets/viewer/elk.bundled.js unmodified. Record in
   assets/viewer/ELK-NOTICE.md: package, version, source URL, the sha256 of the copied file, and that it is used under
   EPL-2.0 (the package is dual "EPL-2.0 OR GPL-3.0-or-later"; we elect EPL-2.0), with the EPL-2.0 notice text / link
   and the Eclipse copyright line from the package. No package.json dependency: the repo stays zero-npm-deps.
2. scripts/layout.mjs (Node >= 18 ESM): reads architecture.model.json (+ optional architecture.layout.json as seeds), runs
   ELK layered with compound zones (zone.parent nesting), deterministic options (fixed seeds, sorted inputs), and writes
   architecture.layout.json: {schemaVersion, graph:{nodes:{id:{x,y,w,h,pinned?}}, zones:{...}, edges:{id:{sections}}},
   er:{entities:{id:{x,y,w,h}}, relations:{...}}}. Seeds: previous positions are fed back so only new or changed nodes move
   ("park" new nodes near their zone, design 14.3). Pinned nodes (layout `pinned: true`) never move. ER view uses one port
   per field row so relation edges attach to the right rows.

tasks.title: Port the viewer core and write render.mjs (clean, internal, shared)
tasks.description:

  focusNode / focusEdge / select / renderDetail; legend chips that toggle relation types and the zone key; renderSeq +

repo-wide denylist test must stay green.

scripts/render.mjs: node scripts/render.mjs <model.json> --layout <layout.json> [--issues <issues.json>]
[--theme <theme.json>] [--mode clean|internal|shared] [--out <file>]. Inlines template, CSS, JS, model, layout (and issues
per mode) into one HTML. clean = default, physically contains no issues; internal = full issues with detail and the global
Issues switch; shared = calibrated summary/impact/fix only. Validate inputs with validate() first.

colour-blind-safe with dash patterns (D10).

tasks.title: prescan.mjs core: inventory, stack detection, area partitioning, generic recipe
tasks.description:
prescan is the 0-token first step of /archmap:build (design sections 6 and 8). Write the core; stack extractors come in
P3.2-P3.4 as plug-ins with a common interface (detect(inventory) -> bool, extract(files, read) -> fragment).
CLI: node scripts/prescan.mjs <repoDir> [--scope <path>] [--out <file>] -> JSON
{schemaVersion, repo, commit (git rev-parse HEAD), stacks[], areas[{id, title, globs[], files, stacks[]}],
 sources[{kind: sqlite|duckdb|..., path, status: found|skipped, reason?}], extracts{<stackId>: fragment}}.
- Inventory: `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard`; skip vendored/generated dirs (node_modules, dist, build, .venv, ...),
  binaries and files over a size cap.
- Partition into <= 8 areas along app/package boundaries (monorepo workspaces, top-level apps, backend vs frontend),
  merging small leftovers. Areas are what the explorer agents get one each.
- Generic recipe: entry points, top-level dirs, Dockerfiles/compose and CI files listed as hints for any stack.
- DB files (*.sqlite, *.db, *.duckdb) are only LISTED here; introspection happens later and never reads rows.
- Deterministic: sorted everywhere, no timestamps in output.
Fixture repos live under tests/fixtures/repos/ and are tiny and FICTIONAL (repo is public). Build test repos with
`git init` in os.tmpdir() from those fixture trees.
